feat: surface the match score on the résumé, and self-host the growth charts (#1063)

* feat(documents): show the match score on the résumé itself

The score surfaces shipped in #1056 were reported missing three times by the
person who asked for them. They were not missing. #1059 and #1060 fixed their
correctness, and on 0.139.3 the owner generated a résumé, screenshotted the
result and said "still i dont see those badges" — because the score lives on the
Job ad tab's Score sub-tab, which JobAdView still describes as "never the
default — that tab is opt-in via an explicit click".

Three PRs fixed correctness and none fixed discoverability, and the original
report was always about discoverability. A surface two deliberate opt-in clicks
away is, to the person who asked for it, indistinguishable from one that does
not exist.

So the number now renders where people look: on the résumé result. Keyword
coverage, the missing-keyword chips, and MatchScore.recommendations — which
Rust has been building as "Consider adding evidence of: …" and which no
component read.

The strip reuses useJobAdTextMatchScore unchanged, so it shares the Score tab's
exact content-addressed cache entry rather than opening a second scoring path.
The job text is snapshotted per completed generation, never wired to live
jobDesc: the Job ad tab next door is an editable textarea and this query is
keyed on the text, so live wiring would mint and fire a fresh scoring call on
every keystroke — through a path that can route via translation, measured at
~117s for one call.

isMeasured / hasScoreCoverage / ScoreMetric move out of JobAdView into a shared
module rather than being copied, so the two surfaces cannot drift on what counts
as a real measurement. Both guards are load-bearing: invoke() does not validate
shape, and `ats: 0` with no gaps means "no extractable keywords" rather than a
genuine zero, which a real 0% would prove by listing every job keyword as a gap.

Never labelled "ATS score" — MatchScore.ats is deterministic keyword coverage
while the analyzer's atsScore is an LLM judgement.

* feat: self-host the star-history and downloads charts

star-history.com stopped drawing a chart. On 2026-06-30 GitHub restricted the
stargazers API to a repo's own admins and collaborators, so the embed now
renders "GitHub restricted access to star data" as an image. The README carried
a sealed_token workaround for exactly this; it no longer helps, and the token
sat in a public file for nothing.

We are the admin, so the data is ours to read: under GITHUB_TOKEN the star+json
media type still returns starred_at for every stargazer. Rendering in-repo
removes a live third-party service from the README and drops the token.

The downloads chart was harder, because there was no data. GitHub reports only a
CURRENT download count per asset, and the badge workflow published to `badges`
as a parentless commit that is force-pushed, so that branch has exactly one
commit and preserved nothing. Two consequences:

  - Going forward, the series has to live INSIDE downloads-history.json. Git
    history on that branch is destroyed by design, every run.
  - The past was recoverable from somewhere else: releases.json, committed daily
    to main by the metrics snapshot, embeds every asset's download_count at that
    moment. Replaying its git history yields 31 real daily readings.

That replay needed a correction rather than a caveat. releases.json is page 1 of
the API and the repo has 139 releases, so only 51 tags ever appeared in a
snapshot and a raw replay sums to 465 against a live 594 — a 129-unit cliff on
the final day that never happened. Releases appearing in no snapshot are counted
once and added as a constant floor. The early points are then an estimate, which
the script says out loud.

The two series are not symmetric and the code is shaped around it: stars are
rebuilt from scratch every run because starred_at is the whole history, while
downloads accumulate because nothing else records them.

The charts are drawn as dark drafting paper, because apps/landing is not a
generic dark site but a notebook — so they reuse its own devices: the
fractalNoise grain overlay, ruled lines with a red margin rule, a hard offset
shadow rather than a soft blur, Patrick Hand, and the stroke-dasharray draw-on
animation from `.draw path`. The line is stroked twice with deterministic
per-point jitter, the way a pencil stroke gets retraced; deterministic because a
fresh wobble each run would make every rebuild a pointless visual diff.

The annotation is the part no other star chart has: the steepest day is found in
the data and labelled in handwriting on a leader line, so the curve says WHAT
happened and not merely that something did.

The finished state is the animation's DEFAULT state, with from-keyframes and a
backwards fill, so a chart can never be hidden by a stylesheet that fails to
apply. The font is inlined as a data URI and the background painted opaque
because web fonts never load through GitHub's camo proxy and
prefers-color-scheme inside an SVG is not honoured there. ~39KB per SVG, free
because the publish target keeps no history.

Folds compute-downloads-badge.mjs into the new script so the badge and the chart
under it cannot print different numbers, and renames the workflow to match what
it now does.

* fix: stop the score strip re-scoring edited text, and never publish reduced history

Nine review findings on #1063, from two reviewers. Each was verified against the
code before being acted on; all nine were real.

Two were caught independently by both reviewers, and both are defects in exactly
the property the strip was built to have:

The snapshot invariant died on a tab switch. GenerationOutput rendered the strip
inside `view === 'doc' && activeOut === 'resume'`, so moving to the Job ad tab
unmounted it and coming back re-ran `useState(jobDesc)` against the LIVE text.
The Job ad tab is where the editable posting textarea lives, so "résumé → job ad
→ edit → back" minted a fresh content-addressed key and fired a scoring call
through a path that can route via translation. The snapshot now lives in
GenerationOutput, which stays mounted across the toggle; the strip owns no state
at all and receives already-snapshotted text.

The CLI-agent egress disclosure was missing. JobAdView renders it on three
branches because a CLI agent reads as "local" everywhere else in this app while
actually egressing the posting text through translation. The strip called the
same hook and the same IPC with no disclosure — and it fires on mount, where the
Score tab needs a click, so the surface that discloses less is the one that
sends more. The notice is now a shared hook used by both.

The remaining renderer findings: `isMeasured` validated two of the four fields it
reads, so a malformed payload would throw a TypeError inside `hasScoreCoverage`
itself — the guard that exists to keep the honest "not scored" state reachable —
and it now validates the arrays too; `ScoreMetric` could print `NaN%` under a red
badge, the exact fabricated-badge bug its header comment warns about, and now
treats non-finite as not-measured. Tests cover the loading, error and
malformed-payload branches, and a regression test pins the snapshot invariant:
mutating the prop back to live `jobDesc` fails it, and nothing else.

The worst finding was in the chart script, in the file whose own comment says the
data is irreplaceable. `readJson` swallowed a parse error into `[]`, and the
workflow force-pushes to a PARENTLESS branch — so one malformed
downloads-history.json would have overwritten the only copy of every reading
since the seed, unrecoverably. It now throws, and the run fails with the last
good file untouched on `badges`. Same rule applied to the stargazer pagination
limit: page 400 coming back full means the API will never hand over the rest, so
it throws instead of quietly publishing a truncated 40,000.

`readJsonArray` and `mergePoints` move to scripts/lib/downloads-history.mjs
because build-repo-charts.mjs fetches the API at import time, so nothing in it
was reachable from a test. Both guards were mutation-checked: reverting the
swallow fails three tests and nothing else.

docs: make the thin-pointer rule reach the agent that writes docs (#1062)

* docs: make the thin-pointer rule reach the agent that writes docs

The rule kept being raised in review because almost nothing enforced it on the
authoring side. Three gaps, all real:

`project-steward` is the SOLE docs writer and loaded no skills at all. Every
other author carries an explicit "First `Read` .claude/skills/…" line — subagents
do not auto-load skills — and this one did not, so `docs-standards` reached an
agent only when someone ran `/update-docs` by hand. Invoked as the docs-sync step
of the implement-workflow, which is the common path, it never saw the rule.

The scopes disagreed. The skill said `docs/knowledge/` points at owning symbols;
reviewers enforce `docs/**`. Agents were following a narrower rule than the one
they were judged against, so the finding was guaranteed to recur on every other
page under `docs/`.

AGENTS.md had no docs rule at all, so Cursor, Copilot and Cline had nothing —
this file is the canonical cross-tool contract and simply omitted the subject.

Adds the self-check that makes the rule actionable rather than aspirational: for
every number or name on a page, ask whether a code change tomorrow would silently
turn it into a lie. If yes, point at where it lives instead.

Also records that a `GENERATED FILE` page is not editable at all — `docs/API.md`
is rendered from the contract TSDoc and `pnpm gen:api:check` fails CI on a hand
edit — so the fix there is always the source, never the page.

Reverts the `.coderabbit.yaml` exception that suppressed this finding on
`docs/API.md`. Owner's call, made knowing it will recur on every PR that touches
an IPC contract: the signal is wanted, and the answer is stricter authoring
rather than a quieter reviewer.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* docs: apply this pr's own premise to the two skills it missed

Four review findings, all correct, and three of them are this PR failing its own
argument.

`project-steward` is write-capable and CLAUDE.md lists it as the docs AUTHOR, yet
it was the only author not reading `author-contract` — whose own first line says
to read it AND your domain standards. It now reads both. `deployment-rules` is
its by frontmatter and was reachable only through `/prepare-release`: the exact
by-hand-only path this PR argues is insufficient for `docs-standards`. Named too.

The narrow scope survived thirty lines below the fix. Line 20 widened the rule to
all of `docs/` while line 53 still said `docs/knowledge/`, so an agent reading the
whole 53-line skill got two scopes and no tie-breaker — worse than the single
narrow rule it replaced. One scope now. The ~150-line cap genuinely IS
`docs/knowledge/`-only, so it is split into its own sentence rather than left
trailing a paragraph about all of `docs/`.

The steward bullet restated the rule verbatim, making a third copy alongside
AGENTS.md and the skill — in the file that forbids copies, in an agent that as of
this PR reads the skill first anyway, and against `token-efficiency`'s "point,
never restate". Collapsed to a pointer. That also drops two motivational lines
from a prompt running on haiku, where length costs adherence.

The CodeRabbit instruction keeps the finding and stops it being unactionable.
The owner asked for the signal back and that stands — nothing is suppressed and
it will still fire on every IPC PR. What was missing is where the fix lives, so
the rule now says a `GENERATED FILE` page is script-rendered and the finding
belongs on the source it renders from. Keyed on the banner, not on `docs/API.md`,
so a second generated page inherits it.

fix(export): give résumé entries the hierarchy they were never structured for (#1061)

* fix(export): give résumé entries the hierarchy they were never structured for

The owner asked for bold company names and a distinguishable duration and got
neither, because the entries were not styled at all — they were never parsed as
entries. The exported text reads

    Independent / Open-Source R&D . Self-directed
    December 2025 – Present, Köln, Deutschland

and `export/parser` recognised three job-entry shapes, ALL of which require the
date on the same line as the title. This shape matched none, so the whole entry
fell through to `LineKind::Text` → `Block::Paragraph` and rendered in plain body
weight. Tuning the styling knobs alone would have been cosmetic.

The parser now also recognises a title line followed by a bare leading date
range, attaching the date and taking the remainder as the subtitle. Guarded by
`is_entry_title_shaped`, and the not-a-heading exclusion is load-bearing: without
it a real section heading followed by a leading-date line reads as "consumed" and
the date is silently dropped. `DATE_RE`'s middle span also had to go greedy so
`.find()` captures the whole range rather than stopping at the first year —
verified a no-op for every other call site, all of which are boolean
`.is_match()`.

Once entries parse, bold falls out: titles were already unconditionally bold and
`emphasize_education` is already hardcoded on, so company, project, education and
certification titles all get it. The date now renders italic rather than
inheriting the title's bold, which is the fast-scan distinction that was asked
for — and no unsafe technique was needed for it: no colour-only signal, no
tables, no letter-spacing.

Italic was never a font problem. All four Carlito faces including italic are
already registered in the Typst `FontBook`; only Regular and Bold were embedded
because no italic run had ever executed. There is now an assertion that a real
italic `/BaseFont` is embedded, so a synthetic slant cannot pass for one.

DOCX carried the same gap in the other direction — its date run was plain while
the PDF's was bold, so the two formats disagreed. Both are italic now, pinned by
an XML-level test asserting `<w:i />` and no `<w:b />`.

`url_label` keeps the full `domain/user/repo` text for a repository URL instead
of collapsing it to "GitHub", matching the reference résumé's bare-domain project
links. A profile URL with a single path segment still collapses.

The header contact line was emitting doubled separators
(`Köln |  · mail ·  | phone`); each raw line's own edge separator is now stripped
before the join.

Scoped to `single_column.typ`, shared by six templates that are all
`TemplateTier::Ats`; the nine bespoke templates are untouched.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(export): stop the new entry branch swallowing a contact line

Four review findings, all valid against HEAD.

The next-line-date branch had no contact guard, and it is checked BEFORE the
`is_contact_shaped` branch that would otherwise claim the line. A header contact
line is title-SHAPED by every other measure — short, unpunctuated, not a heading
— so a contact line followed by a leading-date line became a fabricated job
entry. Reproduced before fixing: "Köln, Deutschland · max@example.de · 0179
1402319" parsed as JobEntry carrying right_text "Jan 2021 – Heute", i.e. the
user's contact details vanish from the header and resurface as a job title.
Every sibling job-entry branch already guarded on this; this one does now too.

The embedded-italic assertion could pass for the wrong reason. Its fixture also
produces italic SUBTITLE runs from location remainders, and `single_column.typ`
renders subtitles italic, so the assertion would have survived the entry date
silently reverting to non-italic. Moved to its own fixture with a date and no
subtitle. Mutation-checked at the right line this time: dropping `style:
"italic"` from the DATE (line 200, not the markdown-italic run at 112) leaves
only Carlito-Bold and Carlito-Regular embedded and fails the test.

The sample-PDF test printed an absolute path. `CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR` makes
`out_path` absolute and both arms passed it to `eprintln!`, against the
path-privacy rule that covers logs explicitly. It prints the repo-relative
artifact name now.

`url_label` kept a URL's query and fragment, so `github.com/user/repo?tab=readme`
would have been printed verbatim on a résumé. Query and fragment are stripped
before the path is split — which also stops a query on a PROFILE link
manufacturing a second segment and promoting it to a repo-shaped label.

fix(match): score non-english postings honestly, and let the score tab run semantic (#1060)

* fix(match): filter stopwords in the posting's own language, not just english

A German posting scored "7% across 291 job keywords" with `abgeschlossenes`,
`abgestimmt`, `abseits` — and `13385`, a Berlin postcode — listed as missing
keywords. Those are function words and a number, not skills, so the coverage
denominator was inflated with them and the percentage meant nothing. For a user
applying to German ads that is every score they see.

`documents::keywords::STOPWORDS` was 89 English words applied unconditionally,
and the token filter admitted anything longer than three characters. The
language plumbing already existed one function away: `make_stemmer` has always
detected the posting language and picked the matching Snowball algorithm. This
reuses that detection to pick the stopword list too, adds curated lists for the
same six languages the stemmer supports, and drops pure-numeric tokens.

Measured on a German fixture, comparing against a helper that reproduces the
pre-fix behaviour rather than against another derived value: coverage 20% -> 29%.

Curation is deliberately incomplete. `agilen`, `academy` and `analysierst` are
left IN the keyword set: an inflated denominator is recoverable, silently
deleting a real skill is not. The French test pins the same residual honestly —
`cherchons` still leaks — instead of hiding it.

MATCH_FORMULA_VERSION 2 -> 3. It is part of `match_scores`' composite primary
key, so old rows become a structural miss rather than a stale hit; every score
recomputes once and nothing needs migrating.

Two subtleties this turned up, both fixed here rather than left as traps:

Per-call `whatlang::detect()` cannot be used for the stopword choice. Short
fragments are not reliably identifiable — the German skills line "Kenntnisse in
Rust, Python, Kubernetes, Terraform und Kafka" reads as ESTONIAN at confidence
0.23 in isolation — so a per-call detection disagreed with the whole-document
language resolved elsewhere, and a filler word survived at one call site while
being absent from the stem->display map built at another, leaking a raw
unstemmed stub into a user-facing message. Call sites that tokenize fragments
(`DocumentTokens`, `Analysis`, `JobVocabulary`) now pass the already-resolved
language explicitly.

`evidence`'s own `FUNCTION_WORDS_DE` is untouched. It answers a different
question (display-only `skills_present`/`skills_absent`) and is deliberately not
formula-pinned. Its guard test needed a new probe word, not a weaker assertion:
`unsere` proved the two filters are independent only while the kernel ignored
it, so the probe is now `profil` — in `FUNCTION_WORDS_DE`, absent from
`STOPWORDS_DE`. The property under test is unchanged.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* refactor(match): split the keyword tests to a sibling file for r8

The stopword work pushed `documents/keywords.rs` to 2303 LOC, past R8's 1400
hard cap, so `cargo test --test architecture` failed. Neither the `--lib` run
nor my own gate caught it, because both of us only ran `cargo test --lib`.

Pure move, no behaviour change: the `#[cfg(test)] mod test` block becomes
`documents/keywords/test.rs`, following the `commands/match_resume.rs` +
`match_resume/` precedent already in the tree. Parent drops to 1155 LOC, the
sibling is 1154, and the 42 keyword tests are unchanged and still pass.

* fix(ai): stop local embeds spending their budget in ollama's queue

Measured on a real machine: embeds failed in exactly 45s cycles — three attempts
at the then-15s bound — while a local 27B chat held the GPU for 213s. Ollama was
UP. It serialises by default, so the embed sat in its queue and its timeout clock
ran the whole time it was queued. Every attempt expired without the request ever
being serviced, and the whole budget bought nothing.

Raising the bound to 30s (this branch's parent) did not change that shape: the
budget was still being spent on queue wait rather than on a request.

Local Ollama chat now maintains an in-flight gauge, and a local embed waits a
bounded OLLAMA_EMBED_QUIET_WAIT for it to clear before dispatching with a FULL
timeout. Busy now degrades in seconds instead of buying three doomed attempts.

Chat is untouched by construction, not merely by test: it only increments and
decrements an atomic behind an RAII guard, and never reads or awaits the gauge,
so its concurrency, ordering and latency cannot change. `tokio::sync::RwLock`
(chat=read, embed=write) was the obvious shape and is WRONG here — tokio's write
lock is fair, so a queued embed would delay the next generation. Verified against
tokio's own source doc rather than assumed. `ollama-cloud` never reaches this
path; it delegates to the OpenAI-compatible client.

A timeout that follows a still-in-flight local chat is now worded distinctly from
a dead daemon, mirroring the timeout-vs-refused split #1051 introduced. A later
change surfaces that state in the UI.

The rerank compile-time assertion is updated, not weakened — the new wait sits
outside the retry budget, so one degraded job now costs
`OLLAMA_EMBED × EMBED_BUDGET_ATTEMPTS + OLLAMA_EMBED_QUIET_WAIT`:
`((30 × 3) + 5) × 3 = 285 < 300`, keeping 15s of margin under
RERANK_STEP_TIMEOUT. Mutation-checked: a 15s quiet wait makes it 315 and fails
the build.

The gauge is process-global, so the tests that touch it are serialised — found
live, when the concurrency test failed under default test parallelism.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* feat(match): let the score tab run semantic scoring

The job-ad Score tab printed "Semantic similarity: Not scored" on every render,
for every posting, forever: `match_resume_text` passed `semantic_enabled = 0`
unconditionally, so `scoreSource` could never be `'combined'` and the row was
structurally unreachable.

It now threads the user's existing `semanticScoring` preference end to end,
mirroring `match:resume` rather than forking a second pattern —
`MatchTextRequestSchema` gains the optional flag, `ipc_contracts/matching.rs` is
REGENERATED (`pnpm gen:ipc`, never hand-edited), and `score_resume_against_text`
takes the bit instead of hardcoding it. No second setting, and it does not
default on.

The query key carries the flag. Without that a keyword-only result is served
under the semantic key the moment the preference flips, and the number silently
contradicts the setting that produced it.

Embeddings matter more here than the English case suggests: they are
language-aware where a stopword list is not, so for a German posting semantic
similarity carries signal that keyword coverage structurally cannot.

Four doc comments were about to become lies and are rewritten with the code:
`MatchSurface`'s axis-2 bullet, `score_resume_against_text`'s and
`match_resume_text`'s docs, `MatchContract.text()`'s TSDoc, and `JobAdView`'s
`hasSemantic` comment plus its "never true through this endpoint" footnote. This
repo has twice shipped a bug that hid behind a comment describing intent while
the code did something else.

Axis 1 is NOT fixed and is kept honest: the Jobs page composes title +
description + requirements, `JobAdView` only ever holds the description, so the
two surfaces still legitimately differ. No parity is claimed that was not
achieved.

`JobAdView.tsx` needed no JSX change — its existing ternary was already correct
once `hasSemantic` became reachable, and the kernel's own "semantic similarity
could not be computed" sentence already surfaced through `explanationText`.
Verified by mutation rather than assumed; the diff there is comment-only.

A degraded embed still yields `scoreSource: 'keyword'` and is not cached under
the semantic key, so a provider outage cannot poison the cache for the whole TTL
— pinned by a test that scores again with the provider back and gets the real
answer.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(validate): stop a truthful german résumé reading as keyword stuffing

The stopword change earlier in this branch made `de_generated_paraphrased.txt` —
a fixture labelled TRUTHFUL — fire `ats.keyword_density`. Caught by
`cargo test --test eval`, which `cargo test --lib` does not build, so neither my
gate nor the authoring agent's saw it.

Filtering a posting's own function words is correct, and it makes documents
shorter in CONTENT tokens. Measured on that fixture rather than reasoned about:

  kernel tokens        89 -> 73
  after this check     82 -> 72
  "backend" x3       3.66% -> 4.17%   (threshold 4%)

An honest résumé saying "backend" three times is not stuffing. The 4% ratio was
calibrated against a denominator inflated with filler; the filler left, so the
calibration had to follow. Two changes, neither of them the threshold itself:

The second filter is gone. `keyword_density_issues` ran kernel tokens through
`function_words` a second time, and its doc said why: "the kernel's own
`STOPWORDS` is English-only". That premise is exactly what this branch fixed.
Worth 7 tokens before, 1 now — redundant, and it was double-shrinking the
denominator. English is unaffected: `function_words("en")` was already empty.

MIN_TOKENS_FOR_DENSITY 50 -> 75, derived not fitted: `3/total > 0.04` holds for
every `total < 75`, so 75 is precisely the point where three ordinary repeats
stops being accusable and four is required. Below it the absolute ceiling of 6
still applies, so real stuffing in a short document is still caught.
MAX_KEYWORD_DENSITY_RATIO and MAX_KEYWORD_OCCURRENCES are untouched.

The pinned-threshold guard is updated WITH the reason rather than silently
re-pinned — moving that number should stay deliberate. Mutation-checked: putting
the floor back to 50 fails `eval` again.

The gate stays `en | de`. The kernel now carries partial lists for fr/es/it/pt/nl,
but partial is the operative word — an uncurated inflected verb form still
survives — so this does not widen an accusation onto the back of a list that is
curated, not exhaustive.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(validate): tokenize density in the resolved language, not a fresh detection

Review catch, and it is a defect I introduced earlier in this branch. Removing
the redundant `function_words(&ctx.lang)` pass left `keywords_normalized_list`
as the ONLY language decision in `keyword_density_issues` — and that variant
re-detects on `generated` alone. Before, the second filter at least used
`ctx.lang`, so I made this strictly worse.

The gate one line above already commits to `ctx.lang`; the tokenizer has to
agree with it. A résumé body is mostly language-neutral tokens, so whatlang has
little to work with: a disagreement silently selects a different stopword
profile, moves the denominator, and can flip whether the issue is emitted.

Tested at the KERNEL level, deliberately, and the reason is worth recording. The
end-to-end version cannot be written honestly: tripping the absolute ceiling
needs a German-only word 7+ times, and that many repeats add enough German
signal to make detection CORRECT again. I wrote that vacuous test three times
before measuring it — each version passed with the fix REVERTED, which is the
only reason I noticed. The kernel test pins the real hazard instead: a tech-dense
body that misdetects as Dutch keeps `wurde` (German-only; Dutch is `werd`) under
the auto profile and drops it under `de`.

Also scopes the CodeRabbit docs thin-pointer instruction away from `docs/API.md`.
That file opens with "GENERATED FILE — DO NOT EDIT", is rendered by
`scripts/gen-api-docs.mjs` from the contract TSDoc, and `pnpm gen:api:check`
fails CI on a hand edit — so the finding it drew was unactionable by
construction, and would recur on every PR that touches an IPC contract. The rule
still applies to every hand-written doc.

fix(documents): score the saved résumé the score tab promises (#1059)

#1057 seeded `resumeDocId` from the default résumé, but only when the seeded text
IS that document's text. That guard is right for the field's own consumer — the
pipeline sends `resumeText: ''` when an id is set, so a mismatched id silently
generates from the wrong résumé — and wrong for the Score tab, which asks a
different question entirely.

The autopilot apply path seeds `applySeedResume: ap.resumeText` (`AutopilotPage`),
a snapshot taken when the autopilot was created. Re-import the résumé and that
snapshot no longer equals the document's text, so the strict guard correctly
declines to seed and the Score tab reads "Save a résumé to score" — permanently,
for every autopilot-originated application. That is the reported symptom.

The tab's own copy already says what it scores: "Scored against your saved
résumé, not the tailored version shown here." So it wants the saved document even

* fix(email): trust only the topmost authentication-results header

The DMARC gate scanned every Authentication-Results header in the message
and accepted a pass from any of them. That header carries no privilege: a
receiving server prepends its own stamp and does not strip ones already
present, so an attacker could add "dmarc=pass header.from=<vendor>" to their
own message and open the write gate by typing a line. Worse than the weak
heuristic it replaced, because the code claimed authentication.

Only the topmost header is read now - the final receiving server prepends,
so anything below it is an earlier hop or sender-supplied text. The ordering
this rests on was verified against mail-parser's source and then proved
empirically with a real two-header message, since a source read can be wrong
about which path runs.

A genuine fail above a forged pass now correctly refuses; that is the case
the old scan got exactly backwards.

One residual stays open and is documented rather than papered over: a lone
forged header copying the expected authserv-id cannot be told from a genuine
one by reading text, and the authserv-id comparison that looks like it would
close it does not - the attacker writes that string too. Real defense is the
provider overwriting inbound headers that claim its identity, which happens

`reachable_chat_model`'s 3s Ollama health probe (in favor of the pure
validate_model check) means an unreachable or busy local daemon now eats the
full completion deadline (minutes, scaled by effort) per translation
attempt instead of a fast skip -- the same run-starving shape this fix's own
commit was written to close. Restores try_state and a should_attempt_translation
gate that gives Ollama alone a cheap reachability check before the call; CLI
agents (newly reachable by this fix, intentionally) have no analogous cheap
probe and proceed regardless.

* fix(ai): sanitize two new tracing:: log sites and split embedding out of documents

documents/mod.rs sat at exactly R8's 1400-LOC hard cap with zero headroom,
bought partly by trimming comments; the next one-line change would fail the
architecture test. Extracts the self-contained embedding round-trip +
posting-vector cache resolver into documents/embedding.rs (re-exported flat
at documents:: so every existing crate::documents::X call site is
unaffected), leaving 185 lines of real headroom.

Also sanitizes two tracing::warn! sites this branch introduced in the same
area (embedding_config's rusqlite::Error read failure, and embed()'s
provider-call failure) -- check-log-error-leaks.mjs only scans log:: macros,
so tracing:: is a blind spot the guard can't see; one of the two wraps a raw
reqwest::Error, and Gemini authenticates via a `?key=` query param.

* fix(ats): stop a non-dash separator from closing an ongoing role

74b95c9f replaced is_open_ended's bare-marker branch with an adjacency
regex whose separator class is [-/] | to | bis | until | hasta | au | a |
tot | fino | ate. A pipe, middot, comma or parenthesis is not in it, and
two callers relied on the old looseness.

tenure.rs::source_is_ongoing answered the one direction its own doc calls
dangerous: "... | 2015 | Present" read as CLOSED, career_span_years
collapsed from 11 to 0, supported_years fell from 13 to 2, and a truthful
"11 years of experience" raised a false factual.inflated_experience
Critical (CRITICAL: user-facing, blocks ok, drives the repair loop to
rewrite correct content). SPAN_MARKER_NO_SEP_RE covered only the
whitespace-only spelling, so it missed every other separator.

Replace it with names_a_present_marker: the marker anywhere on a line the
caller has already established carries a year. No separator list at all -
export::parser::DATE_RE, this codebase's own definition of a job entry's
date range, allows 30 arbitrary characters there, so any enumeration
fails the same way one spelling further out.

Same root cause, second caller: is_date_only reached a separator-free
date column ("..., 2015 Present") only through is_open_ended, so that
column stopped opening a role. Bullets rejoined the entry above, employer
salvage never ran, and unsupported_date_issues - routed through
trailing_date_column by 74b95c9f - went silent on those lines (HIGH, five
consumers). Read PRESENT_MARKERS as a TOKEN there, exactly the way
DATE_ONLY_MARKERS beside it always was; the date_words gate has already
rejected prose, so the restriction protecting is_open_ended is not needed
here. The lists stay disjoint - this reads both, it does not merge them.

The prose leak stays fixed and is re-asserted explicitly: is_open_ended
is unchanged, and the three reported sentences are pinned false.

* fix(egress): require entry-side uniqueness before a sig satisfies an allowlist entry

Content-anchored (sig) matching required exactly one DETECTED LEAK but not
exactly one DECLARED ENTRY, so N allowlist entries sharing a (file, sig) were
all satisfied by the same single leak and the N-1 stale ones were never
reported. A sig could also be satisfied by a leak a DIFFERENT entry already
declares line-exactly, leaving the sig entry with no site of its own and still
counted as live.

Both directions can only ever suppress a stale-entry error, never an
undeclared-leak one: a second site with the same message makes the leak bucket
length 2, which disables sig matching for that bucket outright. Latent today
(one entry uses sig) and live the moment the header's planned mass-sig
migration lands, since duplicated message text is exactly what produces
duplicate sigs.

Entries are now bucketed by (file, sig) the same way leaks are, and a pairing
counts only when both buckets hold exactly one item and the leak is not already
declared by line. Three regression tests cover the two-entry, five-entry and
already-claimed-leak shapes; the existing ambiguous-leak and wrong-file cases
stay as controls. All three fail against the previous implementation.

mutants measured, both survived. Asserting the exact rendered text, which the

ci: group dependabot updates by area, and unblock local pushes (#1050)

* ci: group dependabot updates by the part of the app they touch

Cargo and github-actions only grouped typst and codeql-action, so every
other bump opened its own PR: 5 Rust crates and 4 workflow actions at once.
npm already had a catch-all and collapsed to a single PR.

Adds the same catch-all to both, named for the area so the PR title says
which part of the app moved (desktop-rust, ci-actions), and renames npm's
group to javascript for the same reason. Majors stay individual on all
three, unchanged.

Both catch-alls carry exclude-patterns for the existing lockstep groups.
exclude-patterns beats patterns, so typst and codeql-action stay in their
own PRs regardless of group order in this file - a partial bump inside a
large catch-all PR would not be visible.

npm stays one entry: workspace members share the root pnpm-lock.yaml and
cannot be split per-directory.

* test: move the vitest browser server off a windows-reserved port

Vitest hardcodes defaultBrowserPort = 63315 and allocates upward from
there. Windows reserves blocks for Hyper-V/WSL in that neighbourhood
(63285-63384 here), and a reserved port is still offered by the resolver
but refused at bind, so every push died on:

  Error: listen EACCES: permission denied ::1:63315

with all 6956 tests passing - vitest counts the unhandled error as a
failure. Reproduced identically three times, sandboxed and not.

Pins browser.api.port to 6317, below the dynamic port range where these
exclusions live. The default was already a fixed port, so this is not
trading a dynamic allocation for a static one - it is the same shape at
an address the OS will actually hand over.

Verified: vitest run --project storybook now serves on localhost:6317,
46 files / 180 tests, exit 0.

fix: stop a false language critical and read today as a date column (#1038)

* fix(documents): recognise today/actualidad/oggi/aujourd'hui as date columns

is_date_only used exact-token equality against PRESENT_MARKERS, which never
carried English "Today" or its Spanish/French/Italian equivalents, so an
entry line ending in one of those spellings failed to open its own role and
had its header and bullets absorbed into the entry above it.

Added a separate DATE_ONLY_MARKERS list consumed only by is_date_only rather
than extending the shared PRESENT_MARKERS: that list is also matched by
is_open_ended and validate::content::factual via single-word, no-structure-
required matching, and "today" is common enough English prose vocabulary
that adding it there would risk turning ordinary bullets into false date
contexts (confirmed the same failure mode already live for "actual").
is_date_only requires every token on the line to be a digit, month or
marker, so exact-token equality against a whole date column is safe by
construction regardless of what the list holds.

* fix(documents): widen date-only markers to the currently/presente family

DATE_ONLY_MARKERS only covered the "today" spelling family, so English
"Currently" and the Iberian/Italian "Presente" spelling — both ordinary
CV date-column endings, and Presente reachable via the es/pt/br locale
profiles shipped in #1009 — still failed to open their own role.

Extended the list with the "currently" family (currently, presente,
hoje, atualmente, hoy, actuellement, attualmente, derzeit, vandaag),
kept as literal spellings rather than a shared stem: this const is
already read by a whole-line gate, and nothing stops a future caller
reading it against free text the way PRESENT_MARKERS is, so a prefix
rule would reintroduce the exact hazard the list is separate to avoid.
"nu" (Dutch/Swedish "now") is deliberately left out and documented —
two letters collides far more readily than the rest of the list, and
"heden" already covers the Dutch case.

Measured the tenure.rs path for the same gap (2020 - Atualmente):
career_span_years still reads it as ongoing, because source_is_ongoing
is structural (year + separator + non-year tail) rather than
vocabulary-driven, so no second defect exists there.

* fix(validate): require function-word evidence before a language critical

whatlang's confidence() is a top-1-vs-top-2 margin, not a correctness
probability: a noun-phrase-heavy block (an ordinary skills line, a terse
CV) starves its n-gram model of the closed-class function words it needs
to read a language from at all, so it can land on the wrong Latin-script
language with maximum confidence and is_reliable() == true.

is_language_mismatch now also requires collision-pruned, distinctive
function-word evidence of some other curated language before a confident
Latin-script read becomes an accusation. Non-Latin scripts are unaffected
- whatlang already reads those reliably regardless of function-word
density. The per-section pass now routes through the same function
instead of a duplicated check, closing the same gap at both scopes.

* fix(documents): add spanish actualmente, harden the date-marker tests

Spanish resumes writing an open-ended column as "Actualmente" (one
letter off Portuguese "atualmente", already present) reproduced the
original defect: the header and bullets absorbed into the entry above.
Added the missing spelling and recorded the multi-word-column boundary
(en la actualidad, en cours, ad oggi, bis heute, etc.) as a known,
deliberate limitation rather than a silent gap.

Test hardening from review:

- table test now collects every failing spelling instead of asserting
  inside the loop, so a future dropped/typo'd marker is reported by
  name instead of being hidden behind the first failure
- dropped the paired "prose" loop: every row only passed because the
  tokenizer gate rejects ordinary sentences before any marker is
  consulted, so it proved nothing about DATE_ONLY_MARKERS specifically
  and duplicated a_date_column_needs_more_than_a_year_in_it under a
  misleading name
- added a one-line disjointness assertion so DATE_ONLY_MARKERS and
  PRESENT_MARKERS never silently start sharing a spelling, which is
  the entire safety argument for keeping the two lists separate

Documented a second safety property the review surfaced: since no
DATE_ONLY_MARKERS entry is ever added to PRESENT_MARKERS, a line built
entirely from digits/months/DATE_ONLY_MARKERS tokens still can't pass
is_date_only without a real year or a genuine PRESENT_MARKERS marker,
because looks_like_date_span never consults the new list.

* fix(validate): redesign language evidence as pairwise, not a global pool

Three review findings, all confirmed by measurement:

- a single function-word pool pruned across all seven curated languages
  left Spanish (30 survivors) and Portuguese (33) too thin to evidence
  themselves, so a genuinely Spanish/Portuguese document against another
  target silently stopped raising a real Critical. Evidence is now
  pairwise per comparison (found vs target), not globally pruned.
- short tokens (ci, vi, io, ha, da, ti, os, em, am, im, zu, el, na, ai,
  et, au) collide with common English abbreviations/TLD fragments in
  free text; closed with a named denylist plus curating "per" into the
  English list, rather than a blanket length floor (which was tried
  first and measured to also exclude Italian's own short core
  vocabulary, briefly regressing a true positive).
- the section-scoped pass had its own untested detected_language
  comparison; it now routes through the same is_language_mismatch the
  document pass uses.

Adds a comparative margin (found's evidence must exceed target's own in
the same text) and a title-case-sandwich exclusion (a connector wedged
between two Capitalised words is almost always part of a proper noun's
own official name) to separate "an English document naming a foreign
institution" from a genuine mismatch, without reopening the Spanish
regression. Also fixes the tr/vi corroboration gate to key off Latin
script rather than curated-vocabulary membership, closing a
zero-evidence Critical hole.

* fix(validate): dedupe the portuguese word list, add a duplicate guard

A wider sweep for the zijn-in-NL class of bug found a second instance:
"a" and "se" each listed twice in FUNCTION_WORDS_PT. Harmless under the
current HashSet-based evidence count, but a silent authoring mistake.
Adds a permanent test asserting no curated list has an internal
duplicate, so a third one fails loudly instead of by inspection.

* fix(validate): remove two unproven language-evidence suppressors

Delete AMBIGUOUS_SHORT_TOKENS and distinctive_evidence_confirms's
comparative margin after measuring, for each, that no realistic
document needs it: disabling either left every validate::content
behavioural test green, and only the mechanism's own manufactured unit
test went red. The denylist's one measured trigger required an
adversarial string of disconnected foreign idioms with no connecting
English grammar, a shape this validator's real input never produces,
at a real cost - it permanently denied el/zu/na/et/di/ci, high-
frequency function words of the exact languages the pairwise fix was
written to protect. Removed on the strength of measurement, not kept
on the strength of the argument for them, per this module's own
history.

Replaces the deleted unit tests with ones for the mechanisms that
remain (the single-letter floor, the absolute evidence floor) and
records the measurement in the module doc so a future edit does not
re-add either suppressor without re-measuring.

* fix(validate): replace the title-case sandwich with a measured floor

The title-case-sandwich exclusion in pairwise_evidence_count deleted
German's evidence wholesale: standard German CV register is nominal
("Aufbau und Betrieb der Zahlungsplattform"), German capitalises every
noun, so every connector in that register sits between two capitalised
words whether or not it is inside a proper noun. Both the document and
section passes route through the same function, so this was a single
point of failure with no second line of defence, and it also reopened
the ats/consistency false-positive both already suppress on a language
mismatch.

Deletes the exclusion outright rather than special-casing German - a
shape assumption has now been wrong for Spanish, unfalsifiable for the
denylist, and wrong for German, in three straight rounds. Replaces it
with a threshold, re-derived from a corpus swept fresh for this change
(not carried over from an earlier number): quiet fixtures top out at
4, fire fixtures start at 6, so MIN_DISTINCTIVE_HITS = 5 separates
with a full unit of margin either side. Reports the residual risk
measured at the boundary (an institution-dense English document can
still exceed it) rather than hiding it behind a shape rule.

Adds the missing nominal-register German fixture at both document and
section scope, a Title-Case French fixture, and mutation-checks the
floor at the whole-suite level in both directions. Cross-references
the two same-named FUNCTION_WORDS_DE/function-word primitives in
documents::evidence and validate::content::language so a future reader
does not merge them.

* docs(validate): correct the min_distinctive_hits corpus table and pin two gaps

Round-5 follow-up to bc23ed43, docs and coverage only — no threshold or
mechanism change.

1. The residual-risk paragraph on MIN_DISTINCTIVE_HITS named German's
   institution-stacking case as the worst boundary (five institutions,
   evidence 8). A fresh sweep of French/Italian/Dutch/German with real
   institution names (same shape, one per line, en target) shows German
   is actually the BEST case: even six real German names stay at
   evidence 3, well under the floor. French is the genuinely thin one:
   two real names (INRIA, CNAM) reach evidence 6 at 144 chars, TYING the
   thinnest genuine positive already in the table. Italian crosses at
   five names, landing exactly on the floor (5). Dutch, stacked to the
   same six-name shape as German, also never crosses. Rewrote the doc
   comment with all four measured rows and the honest claim: the margin
   holds for German-shaped proper nouns, not for French or Italian ones.

2. Pinned the close-relative-target silent band as an accepted miss, the
   same discipline this file already applies to the DACH miss and the
   tr/vi miss. Measured: a genuine 120-190 char two-sentence paragraph in
   one Romance language carries far less PAIRWISE evidence against a
   close relative than against a distant target (es-vs-fr: 1; pt-vs-es/
   fr/nl: 4 each — all under the floor) while the SAME text fires
   cleanly against en (6). This repo ships es/pt/it/nl locale profiles,
   so this is a real, supported scenario. New test:
   a_short_paragraph_against_a_close_relative_target_is_an_accepted_miss.

3. per_language_samples()'s round-4 3->7 rep bump for all seven Latin
   languages was load-bearing for the worst pair (es-vs-fr) but left the
   only non-English-target sweep coverage exclusively at 441 characters,
   outside the 120-315 char band the floor actually decides in - exactly
   the gap that hid item 2. Reduced Spanish specifically back to 3x (189

   first to confirm only the es-vs-fr cell goes silent at that length
   (fr: 3, en/de/it/pt/nl: 18/18/15/9/6, all still clearing the floor).
   every_curated_language_is_silent_for_itself_and_fires_for_every_other
   now excludes that one cell explicitly, tied to the new accepted-miss
   test rather than hidden by re-inflating the sample.

* docs: generate the ipc api reference from the contracts

The hand-written docs/API.md documented three namespaces that do not exist

scripts/gen-api-docs.mjs parses packages/shared/src/ipc/contracts with the
TypeScript compiler API and emits the whole page: every namespace, method
signature (verbatim source), TSDoc, channel constant and locally-declared
type. gen:api:check regenerates and diffs, wired into CI's lint-format job.

* docs: move the api reference's hand-written knowledge into contract tsdoc

The old docs/API.md held facts no signature carries: that `intent` picks a
provider's sampling numbers while `temperature` overrides it, that `embed`
chunks and mean-pools and retries a context overflow inside the same call,
that `aiGenerations.save` merge-upserts by jobUrl, that autopilot never
applies, that match is keyword-only unless asked. Each now lives on the
contract member it describes, so the generated page carries it and the code
owns it.

Deliberately not migrated: the enumerated board-id list (already stale
against BOARD_IDS — it missed jobicy) and the `ai:pull-progress` event name
(no such string in the repo). The pointers stay; the copies go.

* docs: point the ipc recipe at the generator instead of the generated page

CONTRIBUTING, the docs-standards skill and the project-steward agent all told
their reader to "document the new namespace in docs/API.md" — the one edit
that file now rejects. They say TSDoc on the contract member, then
`pnpm gen:api`.

* docs: stop the api generator inferring what an empty channel registry means

An empty `*_CHANNELS` const rendered as "this namespace exposes no invoke
channels", which is false: notifications has nine live commands and invokes
their Tauri names directly, as its own doc comment says. Report the
structural fact instead, and state the arithmetic when a registry covers
only some of a namespace's methods.

* docs: send rule 14 to the generator, not to the generated page

docs/API.md is now emitted from the ipc contracts and CI fails on drift, so
the recipe for a new capability has to say where the prose goes — TSDoc on the
contract method — or the next person hand-edits a generated file and loses the
edit on the next run.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(gen-api): fail on duplicate exported names across contract files

The declaration and const maps are keyed by bare name across every contract
file, so a name exported twice silently overwrote the first entry and a
namespace could resolve to another file's interface — rendered under the wrong
heading, plausibly and wrongly. Fail instead of qualifying the key by file: a
real clash is a bug a human should see, not something for the generator to
paper over.

* fix(scripts): diff generated docs against the commit, not the index

`git diff --exit-code -- <file>` compares the working tree to the index, so a
regenerate-and-stage leaves a stale committed copy passing the freshness gate:
it only ever proved the worktree matches whatever was staged. Compare against
`HEAD` so the committed file is what gets checked.

`gen:workflows:check` had the identical hole — it is where the shape was copied
from — so both are fixed here rather than leaving a known-vacuous gate beside a
fixed one.

* fix(gen-api): anchor paths to the script, and keep failures path-free

CONTRACT_DIR, OUT_FILE and repoPath() all resolved against process.cwd(), so
running the generator from anywhere but the repo root read no contracts and
would have written docs/API.md outside the repo. Anchor to the script's own
location, the way packages/shared/scripts/gen-ipc-rust.ts already does.

* feat(scraping): remember which boards actually work between runs

Every scrape already computed a per-board summary and then threw it away
everywhere except the last autopilot run, so a board broken since Tuesday
looked exactly like one that simply found nothing today.

Each run now folds its summaries into a new `scraping::board_health` store and
attaches the derived verdict to the summary the renderer already receives, so
the existing chips gain a second amber chip - "down for 4 runs, last worked 6
days ago" - beside the board's own result. Nothing is ever suppressed: a
failing board still runs on the next search.

The table holds exactly one row per board, upserted, so it is bounded by the
scraper registry rather than by time - there is no retention window to age out
and nothing to prune. A skip is kept structurally distinct from an error: a
board that was never contacted advances neither the verified timestamp nor the
failure streak, and does not clear an existing one. A cancelled run records
nothing at all, so a user's own cancel cannot manufacture a streak.

The correlation id is the scrape job id that already existed; none is minted.
The new summary field is serde-optional, so records persisted before this - and
every backup bundle carrying them - still deserialize.

* fix(scraping): rescale the decayed failure tally in u64, not u32

Found by the architecture audit of the decay commit, and it falsified that
commit's own doc comment.

`failed.saturating_mul(next_verified)` overflows u32 once the product passes
~4.29e9, and saturating_mul clamps BEFORE the divide. That destroys exactly the
proportionality the function exists to preserve: a board that failed 150_000 of
200_000 runs decayed to 2-in-12, read 16%, and came out HEALTHY. The doc
comment claimed the rescale handles an "arbitrarily large" legacy tally; it did
not.

after every call, so the magnitude needed is ~131_072. It is reachable from a
hand-edited row, which is the same threat model this module already defends
against for a negative tally. Defending one sibling and not the other is how a
landmine outlives the person who knew about it.

The existing oversized-tally test could not catch this: it asserts only that
the cap is respected, and the cap IS respected while the ratio is being
destroyed. The new test anchors on an absolute floor instead — a board failing
three runs in four must not decay to something better than a coin flip. 75%
legitimately erodes to ~67% across the 14 halvings, because floor-scaling only
ever rounds down; 16% is the bug. Mutation-checked by execution: restoring the
u32 arithmetic reproduces 2/12 = 16% and the test goes red.

Also records what FLAKY_WINDOW_CAP does NOT say. It bounds RUNS, not time. At
the daily autopilot cadence that is one to two weeks, close to STALE_AFTER_MS;
for someone scraping manually several times an afternoon the same 16 runs span
hours, and the verdict forgets the morning by evening. That is the honest
behaviour of a counter with no clock, but nothing said so.

shipped: curl sends no Origin, so it never exercises CORS at all.

scrub-engine loads each clip with `fetch(url).then(r => r.blob())` and hands the
blob to a video element. That is a cross-origin request, and GitHub release
downloads carry no `Access-Control-Allow-Origin`, so every clip fetch threw and
the engine fell back to its poster stills. The page looked fine and had no
video.

R2 fixes the actual constraint rather than working around it: a bucket can
declare a CORS policy, so the response carries the header the engine needs.
Egress is unmetered there, so the Pages bandwidth ceiling that move was chasing
is gone rather than relocated. The objects went up with
`cache-control: public, max-age=31536000, immutable`, which is honest because a
new clip set means new keys rather than mutated ones.

Verified against the live origin this time, not with curl: a real
`fetch().then(r => r.blob())` from the deployed site returns 200 and a
2,503,061-byte video/mp4 blob that produces a working object URL. Headers
checked directly too, and the allow-origin header is present for this origin
and absent for a disallowed one.

The tests now pin the HOST, not just the URL shape, because that is where the
defect lived: a same-origin `/world/vid/...` path and a GitHub release URL both
look correct and both break the route. Mutation-checked by execution against
each of those two states in turn; each turns three tests red.

localhost:3000 is on the bucket's CORS allowlist, so plain `next dev` works
without the NEXT_PUBLIC_WORLD_VIDEO_BASE override.

refactor(landing): serve the /world clips from a release, not from the repo (#1031)

33 files, 62 MB of video leave the tree for the `world-assets-v1` release. Two
separate problems, one move.

Git weight. Video does not delta-compress, so a re-encode writes every byte
again rather than a diff, and one re-encode round had already put roughly 38 MB
of unreclaimable history in the pack. Keeping the clips here meant every future
re-encode cost its full size forever.

Bandwidth. Sitting in apps/landing/public/ meant they were built into the Pages
site, so every view drew on the Pages 100 GB per month soft limit. At this
route's 20 MB device-set cap that is about 5,000 visits a month, which is low
enough to actually reach. Release assets are a different pool, documented with
no limit on size or bandwidth.

The poster stills stay, deliberately: about 2 MB, and they must paint before
anything is fetched. The published site drops from about 74 MB to 12 MB.

Every clip URL now goes through one `vid()` helper pinned to a release TAG.
Pinning is the point: publishing world-assets-v2 and bumping one line is atomic,
whereas mutating an existing release's assets would leave cached clients
disagreeing with fresh ones. `NEXT_PUBLIC_WORLD_VIDEO_BASE=/world/vid` restores
local files for offline work, and the directory is gitignored so a local copy
cannot be re-committed by accident.

The two tests that asserted every asset path starts with `/world/` split in
two, because that invariant now holds for the posters and not for the clips.
Both halves assert against LITERALS rather than against the config's own base,
so a regression cannot move the expectation along with the value; a fourth test
pins every clip to one tag so a partial bump cannot ship. Mutation-checked by
execution: pointing the base back at /world/vid turns two of them red.

* feat(validate): catch invented tenure, certifications and education

Three invention classes the metric family cannot see, wired in with the tiers
the calibration commit measured rather than the tiers their names suggest.

factual.inflated_experience (Critical). Compares the NUMBER in "8+ years of
experience" against what the source states in words and against the span its
own employment dates cover, plus one year of slack for the months a year column
does not carry. Only an OVERSTATEMENT fires: rounding down is not a fabrication,

near it is not a credential, so "certified the release each Thursday" reports

* feat(match): report hard constraints beside the score instead of blending them into it

Track E1 of the architecture audit.

`combined = f(semantic, ats)` measures how much of a posting's vocabulary the
résumé carries. It is a good relevance number and it structurally cannot answer
"could I actually take this job?", so a candidate who fails a non-negotiable
still scores well on keyword overlap. The fix is not to fold a penalty into the
number — it is to answer the second question separately.

`match_resume` now returns a `constraints.checks` field beside the score. Three
rules hold it up:

* it never touches the score. The verdict is computed in the L3 command AFTER
  the kernel returns, so it is not an input to `score_one` and never enters the
  `match_scores` cache — whose key is composed of SCORING inputs only, and would
  therefore have served a stale verdict for a whole TTL the moment the user
  edited their preferences. Out here, a cache HIT still gets a fresh verdict,
  and the Autopilot and extension entry points that share the kernel are
  byte-identical;
* it never hides a job. Nothing filters, sorts or gates on it. A wrong knock-out
  tells the user not to bother applying, which costs far more than a wrong
  percentage;
* absence of evidence is never evidence. `ConstraintStatus` has FOUR values, and
  the two "we don't know" ones are distinct from both a pass and a fail:
  `unknown` (the candidate stated a preference, the posting says nothing, or
  what they stated is not comparable) and `noPreference` (the candidate has
  expressed nothing at all — differently actionable, since the user can fix that
  one). A `notMet` requires positive evidence on BOTH sides, and each check
  carries each side's own words so that is a checkable property of the payload
  rather than a promise. It is enforced inside the one constructor every check
  goes through, not as a post-pass a later constraint could skip.

ONE constraint ships, because one is what the app has honest candidate-side data
for. `location`: the user's stored job-search location (and its geocode-picked
country code) against the posting's location text and its board remote flag.
Both sides are real, persisted, user-entered data.

The audit's other three are refused, and the module says so in full:

* work authorization, ranked first, has NO candidate-side field anywhere — not
  on the contact profile, not in job preferences. The tempting proxy, the
  candidate's own address, is exactly the false accusation this repo already has
  a live incident from: living in one country is not evidence of lacking
  authorization in another;
* employment type has no persisted preference. `AutopilotTarget::work_type` is a

running:

1. DATA LOSS. The last-search signature (and its replace latch) reset to '', so

   replace:true, which clears the persisted postings cache the moment the first
   item streams. "Show more", whose entire contract is APPEND, destroyed the
   user's result set. The scrape FORM reset with it, so restoring only the
   signature would not have been enough: the criteria differed too, and the

   the next search failed to supersede the orphan - two scrapes writing into one

   explanation of an empty result) were dropped, and dropped again when a scrape
   finished while the user was elsewhere.

All of it moves into JobsSlice, which already held listScrollTop for exactly

fix(autopilot): jitter scheduled runs so default installs stop herding (#1018)

Track B3 of the architecture audit.

Schedules are clock-anchored, the tick is 60 s wide, and every record created
before the run-time picker defaults to 09:00. So every default-schedule install
in a time zone hits the same third-party APIs inside the same minute. This is
not theoretical here: the desktop log already shows scheduled runs failing with
`adzuna: HTTP 503`.

The offset is DETERMINISTIC per autopilot, derived from its id, not random —
that is the whole design. A random delay would have meant sleeping inside the
tick, which breaks the two properties everything else is built on: catch-up
after a missed occurrence, and no-double-run once `lastRunAt` is stamped at or
after the occurrence. Shifting the OCCURRENCE instead keeps it a single
well-defined instant, so both still hold, and tests stay reproducible.

FNV-1a rather than `DefaultHasher`: the standard hasher is explicitly not stable
across Rust releases, and an offset that moved on a toolchain bump would
silently shift every user's schedule. Ids are UUIDs, so the low bits are already
well distributed.

Ten minutes: wide enough to spread a herd across ten tick windows, far enough
under the shortest interval (hourly) that a shifted occurrence can never
overtake the next one, small enough not to surprise someone who picked 09:00.
That upper bound is a `const _: () = assert!(...)` beside the constant rather
than a test — a test comparing two constants is a tautology clippy rejects, and
this makes a bad value unbuildable instead of merely reported.

Tests cover the offset being stable for an id and inside the window, the
occurrence moving by exactly the offset, and the behaviour a user would notice:
between the nominal time and the offset, today's occurrence has NOT been reached,
so the latest is still yesterday's. Plus a full-day minute-by-minute sweep
asserting exactly one transition — one run per day, no double-run, no skip.

Mutation-checked: making the offset always zero fails
`jitter_actually_spreads_a_herd` with "200 autopilots landed in only 1 distinct
minutes".

  'idle' — and `inProgress` is deliberately not badged, so nothing else on the

  the user was away, terminal `complete` included, was dropped;
* `runAutopilot`'s `onSuccess` invalidation belongs to the unmounted observer,

  no local state for an autopilot, so the card shows 'scraping' and the Run
  button stays disabled;
* let the machine's `idle` accept the mid-run vocabulary, not just the start —
  a card that rejoins mid-run gets `scrape_done`/`complete` with no preceding
  `scrape_start`, and dropping those pinned it back to idle;
* let the terminal states re-arm on `scrape_start`, so the scheduler's next
  occurrence doesn't stream underneath a card frozen on the last outcome;
* invalidate the list when a run ends, which also fixes scheduled runs never
  showing their results until the next navigation;
* stop reverting to 'idle' on `already-running`. That refusal is proof a run is

* ci: enforce the rust toolchain pin instead of asking for it in a comment

The pin itself already shipped and is correct: `rust-toolchain.toml` pins
1.97.1, and both `dtolnay/rust-toolchain` uses are pinned to the SHA for that
same version. What was missing is any enforcement.

The two halves cannot reference each other — that action does not read toolchain
files, its `@rev` IS the version selector — so the only thing tying them
together was a comment in three files saying "bump both together". That is the
shape this repo treats as a defect: a stated invariant with nothing checking it.

The failure is quiet, which is what makes it worth a check. Bump the TOML alone
and CI keeps building on the old compiler; bump the action alone and every
developer's machine drifts off what CI validates. Neither goes red on its own —
the pin simply stops meaning anything, which is exactly the state it was created
to end.

`scripts/check-toolchain-pin.mjs` asserts four things: the channel is an exact
three-part version rather than a floating one; every `dtolnay/rust-toolchain`
use under `.github/` carries a trailing `# <version>` comment (an opaque SHA is
unreviewable by construction, so the comment is load-bearing, not decoration);
every one of those declared versions equals the channel; and the Cargo MSRV is
not above the pin, since that pairing cannot compile at all.

It deliberately does NOT verify that the SHA truly is that version — that needs
a network call, and it is not the mistake people make. The realistic error is
updating one place and forgetting the other, which is fully catchable offline.

Wired into the `lint-format` job, which has no path filter and so runs on every
PR — a toolchain drift guard that only fires when Rust files change would miss
the case where someone edits only the workflow. The three comments now name
their enforcer instead of asking nicely.

Guard is mutation-tested five ways against the real repo (bump either half
alone, float the channel back to `stable`, strip a version comment, raise the
MSRV past the pin) — all red, tree restored clean — plus 11 black-box CLI tests
over a fake repo tree, following `check-tech-radar.test.mjs`. One of those
covers removing CI's pin entirely, which would otherwise pass vacuously: with
nothing to compare, nothing disagrees.

Issue #1002, opened by freehire's maintainer, who disclosed the interest. We
publicly committed to shipping it in the next release.

Implemented from their published openapi.yaml rather than from the PR they
offered. The reason is rights, not code quality: this repo has no CLA, so a
contribution stays under its author's copyright and cannot be relicensed, and
ADR-023 names commercial licensing as a rationale. Reading their PR and
rewriting it would be derivative — the worst of both worlds — so the spec is
the only source used.

What it buys: every other provider needs an API key, so a fresh install gets a
needs-keys skip and zero jobs. freehire answers unauthenticated, so the
aggregator board can return results before the user has configured anything.
It is not a better source than the keyed tiers and is never preferred over
one — it runs LAST, after Adzuna, JSearch and Jooble have each failed to
produce a decisive result, and only a non-empty answer from it short-circuits.
An empty answer from a provider nobody chose is not evidence about the search,
so it must not swallow a configured provider's failure diagnostic.

Two consequences worth calling out rather than burying:

`needs_keys()` is now always false, because a keyless tier is always
"configured". That is the point — the skip existed because a keyless search
could only ever return nothing. The cost, accepted and tested: a keyless user
whose freehire search finds nothing reads "no jobs found" rather than a prompt
to add keys. A keyring READ FAULT is still classified separately, so the one
case the old `false` protected is unaffected.

Failures degrade to Ok(empty), never Err — the only provider with that rule.
Every other one reports its failure because a stored key means the user asked
for it specifically. Nobody opted into this one, so surfacing its outage would
turn a third party's downtime into an error banner on a search the user never
aimed at them. There is no SLA and no rate-limit header of any kind (verified:
no X-RateLimit-*, no Retry-After), so it is treated as always-possibly-absent.

Uses the documented /agent/jobs/search with `q` and
`description_format=markdown` — NOT the undocumented /jobs/search taking
`query`, which is what the issue described and what a first pass reached for;
building from the published spec is the whole basis for implementing this
ourselves. Markdown up front is also what keeps scoring from needing a
per-result detail fetch.

A guessed country is deliberately not sent as a filter: the aggregator defaults
`country` to "de" when the caller supplied none, and pinning a keyless tier to
that guess would reproduce the guessed-market bug already fixed for Adzuna.
`location` is unused because the documented search has no city parameter at
all, and folding a city into the full-text `q` would drop every posting that
does not spell its city out, remote ones included.
